scope: static demand; target timing and quality are not measured

terms.note: every supply figure here is a bound on a quantity a composition declares and not a value: the two bandwidth figures are minima on what must be granted and measured, the payload is a minimum and tau a maximum, so the usable payload floor is 3.2 GB and a composition may declare more. A demand above any of them is met by a composition above the floor and fails only against one at it.
terms.unit_base: decimal, 10^9 bytes per GB. R-18-004b fixes no base for its unit and the corpus writes the second-class region in binary units elsewhere, so the base is this report's convention; against a binary 4 GiB payload every multiple of the usable payload floor falls by a factor of 1.0737
terms.kv_cache_class: undecided by any artifact. R-18-004a(vii) places the model wholly on the second class and says nothing about the cache; R-15-247s's second list names model weights and bulk by volume and names no cache, and its criterion is latency-criticality, which a cache read once per generated token can be argued either side of. The placement is the whole-program memory plan's (R-08-012a), so every demand and resident figure below that folds K in is an upper bound conditional on the cache sitting on the second class, and weights_only_demand_gb_per_second beside it is the part R-18-004a(vii) does place there

arithmetic: same Q4a budget: rate * (weight stream + KV at context); resident = tensor bytes + KV + logged compute MiB * 2^20 + one f32 vocabulary row
precision: compute MiB is printed to two decimals; resident carries its half-unit rounding interval, not a claim of exact allocated bytes
